J. Harden |year=1993 |work= PlantNET - NSW Flora Online |access-date=15 June 2011}} is an [[evergreen]] [[Australia]]n plant. A shrub to 5 metres tall found in wet [[sclerophyll]] forest and [[rainforest]], usually on the coastal lowlands. From near [[Bilpin, New South Wales]] further north to [[Queensland]]. ''C. stricta'' has become [[naturalisation (biology)|naturalised]] in [[Victoria (Australia)|Victoria]].{{GRIN | access-date=15 June 2011}} == Description == Leaves are long and thin, 30 to 50 cm long, 1 to 2 cm wide. Mauve flowers form on [[panicle]]s, 20 to 40 cm long. The flowering stem is 15 to 30 cm long. Fruit are purple to black, 10 to 15 mm in diameter. This is the only Australian species of ''Cordyline'' with black fruit. [[File:Cordyline.stricta.jpg|thumb|alt=Narrow-leaved palm lily (Cordyline stricta) also known as the Slender Palm Lily|Narrow-leaved palm lily (Cordyline stricta)]] == Uses == === Cultivation === ''Cordyline stricta'' is widely planted in gardens and commercial landscapes for the ornamental value of both its foliage and flower heads and berries. Its tall, narrow growth makes it useful as a screen plant. ''C. stricta'' is adaptable to a wide range of climate and planting situations, from full sun to shade, and is moderately drought tolerant once established. It does not tolerate frost well.{{Cite web|title=Cordyline stricta|url=https://anpsa.org.au/plant_profiles/cordyline-stricta/|access-date=2022-10-03|website=Australian Native Plant Society|date=October 2013}} === Ecological === ''Cordyline stricta'' is a [[host (biology)|host plant]] for [[Sabera dobboe|Yellow-streaked Swift caterpillars]]. == References == {{Reflist}} {{Taxonbar|from=Q5170123}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Cordyline stricta}} [[Category:Cordyline|stricta]] [[Category:Plants described in 1825]] [[Category:Flora of New South Wales]] [[Category:Asparagales of Australia]] [[Category:Flora of Queensland]] [[Category:Butterfly food plants]] [[Category:Garden plants of Australia]]
